'''''Bromus racemosus''''', the '''smooth brome''' or '''bald brome''', is a species of flowering plant in the family [[Poaceae]].<ref>{{cite web |title=''Bromus racemosus'' smooth brome |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/105541/i-bromus-racemosus-i/details |date=2021 |publisher=The Royal Horticultural Society |access-date=14 September 2021 }}</ref> It is native to subarctic and temperate Eurasia, and widely introduced elsewhere, including North America, Iceland, the [[Southern Cone]] of South America, the Korean Peninsula, Australia, and New Zealand.<ref name="394050-1" >{{cite web |url=http://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:394050-1 |title=''Bromus racemosus'' L. |author=<!--Not stated--> |website=Plants of the World Online |publisher=Board of Trustees of the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew |access-date=14 September 2021 }}</ref> It grows in alkaline meadows and in waste places.<ref>{{cite book |title=CRC World Dictionary of Grasses. Common Names, Scientific Names, Eponyms, Synonyms, and Etymology |last1=Quattrocchi |first1=Umberto |year=2006 |isbn=9781420003222 |page=387 }}</ref>

==Description==

''Bromus racemosus'' is an annual grass growing {{cvt|17-60|cm}} tall. Its smooth [[Culm (botany)|culm]]s are {{cvt|1-2.1|mm}} wide at their base. Its brown nodes are minutely to densely pubescent, with these soft and wavy hairs growing up to {{cvt|1.2|mm}} long. Its membranous and glabrous [[ligule]]s are {{cvt|0.5-2|mm}} long. Its leaf blades are {{cvt|2.7-12|cm}} long and {{cvt|1-3|mm}} wide; the adaxial surface of the blade is densely covered by stiff hairs growing up to {{cvt|0.8|mm}} long, and the abaxial surface is densely covered with stiff hairs which are typically shorter, growing up to {{cvt|0.6-0.8|mm}}. The margins of the blades are smooth or serrulate. Its [[panicle]]s are {{cvt|3-8.5|cm}} long and {{cvt|1-2.5|cm}} wide, with erect to ascending branches which range between scabrous and pubescent. Each branch has a single [[spikelet]], with the lowest [[inflorescence]] node having one to four branches. The ovate-lanceolate spikelets are {{cvt|1.5-2.2|cm}} long, with the rachilla occasionally visible at maturity. The spikelets have six to nine florets. Its [[glume]]s are smooth or scabrous, with lower glumes {{cvt|5.2-6.7|mm}} long and upper glumes {{cvt|6.2-8.5|mm}} long. The lower glumes have three to five nerves, upper glumes have seven to nine nerves, and [[Lemma (botany)|lemma]]s have seven to nine nerves. Its lemmas are {{cvt|6.5-9.5|mm}} long, and its [[Awn (botany)|awn]]s are {{cvt|3.4-8.5|mm}} long.<ref name=Texas>{{cite journal |pages=349–350 |journal=Journal of the Botanical Research Institute of Texas |title=Taxonomy of Bromus (Poaceae: Pooideae: Bromeae) Sections ''Bromopsis'', ''Bromus'', and ''Genea'' in British Columbia, Canada |last1=Saarela |first1=Jeffery M. |volume=2 |number=1 |year=2008 |publisher=Botanical Research Institute of Texas |editor=Barney L Lipscomb |url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/41650331#page/358/mode/1up}}</ref>

==Habitat and distribution==

In its native Europe, ''Bromus racemosus'' occurs in moist meadows and [[grassland]]s, though it is threatened by changes in agricultural grassland management.<ref>{{cite journal |title=Habitat and management preference of Bromus racemosus L., a rare species in mesic meadows of Northwest Europe |author=Simmelink, Max R and Janssen, John and Schamine, Joop HJ and Weeda, Eddy J |journal=Tuexenia |volume=37 |pages=289–312 |year=2017}}</ref> In its introduced habitat in North America, ''B. racemosus'' occurs in waste places, fields, roadsides, and gravelly hills in scattered locations throughout the United States and Canada.<ref name=Texas/> In South America, the grass occurs in the southern [[Andes]] of Argentina and Chile.<ref>{{cite book |author=Wilson |first=K.L. |title=Monocots: Systematics and Evolution |last2=Morrison |first2=D.A. |publisher=CSIRO |year=2000 |isbn=9780643063938 |page=94}}</ref>
